ORDER

1. The present Application is filed under Section 9 of the Insolvency and 
Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (‘the Code’) read with Rule 6 of the Insolvency 
and Bankruptcy (Application to Adjudicating Authority) Rules, 2016 by 
Cornish Aluminium India Pvt. Ltd. (‘Operational Creditor’), against the 
Corporate Debtor for the purpose of initiating Corporate Insolvency 
Resolution Process (‘CIRP’) against M/s Neo Nitika Projects Pvt Ltd.  
(‘Corporate Debtor’). 
2. The Operational Creditor, i.e., M/s. Cornish Aluminum India Pvt. Ltd. (CIN: 
U52100DL2010PTC208292) is a Private Limited Company incorporated 
under the Provision of the Companies Act, 1956 and is engaged in the 
business of providing vast range of scaffolding & shuttering equipment 
for industry and construction. The Registered Office of the Operational 
Creditor is at Shop No. 311, T/F. Plot No. 192, Mamaram East Plaza, 
Mayur Vihar, Phase - 3, New Delhi -110096.  
3. The Corporate Debtor i.e., M/s. Neo Nikita Projects Pvt. Ltd. (CIN:  
U45200DL2009PTC186278) is a Private Limited Company incorporated 
under the Provision of the Companies Act, 1956 and is engaged in the 
real estate and construction industry. The Registered Office of the 
Corporate Debtor is at PVT No. 206, H. No. 29G, Ward No. - 1, 1st Floor, 
Mehrauli, New Delhi - 110030. 
Case of the Applicant/Operational Creditor 
4. The Corporate Debtor approached the Applicant Company through its   
Director/Authorized Representative in requirement of scaffolding and 
shuttering equipment on hiring basis for construction purposes. The 
parties executed a Rental Agreement dated 11.04.2016 for supply of 
scaffolding materials on a hiring basis wherein the Corporate Debtor 
agreed that it would make full payment of agreed rents on time.

Page 3 of 18 
C.P. (IB) –28(ND)/2025 
Date of Order: 02.12.2025 
5. Accordingly, the Applicant Company supplied scaffolding materials to the 
Corporate Debtor at following project sites of the Corporate Debtor: 
i. Neo Nitika Projects Private Limited, AJNARA, GH-08, Sector 79, 
Noida, Uttar Pradesh. 
ii. Neo Nitika Projects Private Limited, AMBROSSIA, Sector 118, Naida, 
Uttar Pradesh. 
iii. Neo Nitika Projects Private Limited, COSMOS, GH-0lC, Sector 16, 
Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. 
iv. Neo Nitika Projects Private Limited, MAHAGUN, Sector 16, Greater 
Noida, Uttar Pradesh. 
v. Neo Nitika Projects Private Limited, SAMRIDHI LUXURIA, Sector 105, 
Noida, Uttar Pradesh. 
6. It is submitted that the Applicant Company raised invoices and demand 
notes for the scaffolding material and maintained separate ledger 
accounts for all the above-mentioned sites. Subsequently, the Corporate 
Debtor started defaulting in making payments of amounts payable under 
respective invoices on their respective dates despite repeated requests 
and reminders. The conduct of the Corporate Debtor is totally 
unprofessional and contrary to the terms and conditions as enumerated 
in Rental Work Order dated 11.04.2016. 
7. It is submitted that as on 23.08.2023, total outstanding amount is Rs. 
1,15,43,684.49/- which has been calculated after deducting excluding 
invoices from period  25.03.2020 to 24.03.2021, i.e., suspended period 
due to Covid 19 Pandemic. Such debt fell due from the respondent 
concern excluding interest towards the services rendered to it by 
Operational Creditor. The details of the debt and the date from which 
such debt fell due is herein below: 
(a) The total outstanding amount to be recovered qua AJNARA 
site including interest from the Corporate Debtor is Rs. 
5,80,902/- which includes an amount of Rs. 5,47,677/- against 
invoices raised for the period 31.08.2016 to 01.11.2018 and the 
cost of the material supplied of Rs. 33,225/-.

(b) The total outstanding amount to be recovered qua 
AMBROSSIA site including interest from the Corporate Debtor is 
42,50,269/- which includes an amount of Rs. 36,82,214/- 
against invoices raised for the period 31.08.2016 to 01.08.2022 
and the cost of the material supplied of Rs. 5,67,995/-.  
(c) The total outstanding amount to be recovered qua COSMOS 
site including interest from the Corporate Debtor is Rs. 
16,32,713/- which includes an amount of Rs. 15,80,563/- 
against invoices raised for the period 31.08.2016 to 01.08.2022 
and the cost of the material supplied of Rs. 52,150/-. 
(d) The total outstanding amount to be recovered qua MAHAGUN 
site including interest from the Corporate Debtor is 37,13,556/- 
which includes an amount of 32,22,198/- against invoices raised 
for the period 21.04.2016 to 31.03.2019. Moreover, outstanding 
rental amount against material supplied is Rs. 4,91,358/-. and 
the cost of the material supplied of Rs. 33,225/-. 
(e) The total outstanding amount to be recovered SAMRIDHI 
LUXURIA site including interest from the Corporate Debtor  is 
10,90,756/- which includes an amount of 7,04,656/- against 
invoices raised for the period 01.02.2020 to 31.08.2022 and the 
cost of the material supplied of Rs. 3,86,100/-. 
8. The Corporate Debtor in partial discharge of its admitted liability for the 
total outstanding amount towards the payment of rental of materials 
handed over two cheques to the applicant.  The details of the cheques 
are: - 
i. Cheque No. 557979 dated 31.08.2022 for a sum of Rs. 
37,60,200/- drawn on Punjab National Bank, West Vinod 
Nagar, Mandawali, Delhi - 110092. 
ii. Cheque No. 074230 dated 31.08.2022 for a sum of Rs. 
8,00,000/- drawn on Punjab National Bank, West Vinod Nagar, 
Mandawali, Delhi - 110092.

9. The Corporate Debtor assured the applicant that the said cheques would 
be honoured at the time of presentation. The Applicant presented the said 
cheques for encashment in its bank account at IndusInd Bank, 1st 
Floors, Antriksh Plaza, Plot No. 2, Sector 10, MLU, Dwarka, New Delhi -  
110075 on 01.09.2022, however, the said cheques got dishonoured and 
with the return memo dated 02.09.2022 from its banker with remarks 
"Account Blocked". Being aggrieved, the Applicant company sent legal 
notice dated 26.09.2022 calling upon Corporate Debtor to pay against 
outstanding payment against the invoices, outstanding rental amount 
and also to return the scaffolding material supplied by Applicant 
Company to Corporate Debtor along with  interest @ 24% per annum till 
final payment. However, the Corporate D ebtor did not reply to the said 
legal notice. 
10. The Applicant Company wrote multiple e-mails from the year 2020 to 
2023 for the payment of outstanding rental amount and return of 
scaffolding material. Further, the Operational Creditor also contacted 
Corporate Debtor telephonically for payment of outstanding rental 
amount but the Corporate Debtor never responded for the payments. 
Despite repeated follow ups and correspondence by Operational Creditor, 
Corporate Debtor failed to make outstanding payment against the 
invoices and outstanding rental amount to the Operational Creditor. 
Moreover, Corporate Debtor also failed to return the scaffolding material 
to Operational Creditor. 
11. It is submitted that even after more than 30 reminders sent to the 
Corporate Debtor, no response was received by the Operational Creditor. 
Thereafter, the Operational Creditor issued a Demand Notice dated 
20.11.2023 under Section 8 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 
2016 sent through speed post dated 21.11.2023 to the Respondent/  
Corporate Debtor. Despite the receipt of the demand notice, the 
Corporate Debtor neither replied nor made the payment of the total due 
amount. Hence, the present application.

C.P.(IB)-28(ND)/2025 
Date of Order-02.12.2025 
Page 6 of 18  
Submissions of the Corporate Debtor/Respondent 
12. The Corporate Debtor has filed Reply Affidavit dated 26.05.2025 denying 
the averments and contentions raised by the Applicant and submitted 
that the present application is not maintainable and deserves to be 
dismissed on the following grounds: -  
A.  PETITIONER IS NOT ENTITLED TO MAINTAIN PETITION 
It is submitted that the Petitioner failed to comply with the conditions laid 
under Section 9(3) of the Code, particularly sub-clauses (c) and (d), relating 
to delivery of invoices and certificate of no payment.  Furthermore, the 
presence of a civil dispute and the necessity for detailed adjudication on 
facts and forgery indicates that this matter lies outside the purview of a 
Summary Insolvency Proceedings under Section 9. 
B. THE INSTANT CASE IS A CLEAR CASE OF PRE-EXISTING DISPUTE 
It is submitted that in the present case, there exists a pre-existing dispute 
which is evident from the following facts: - 
i. Wrongful calculation of charges at Rs. 60/kg instead of agreed Rs. 36/kg 
It is submitted that the Work order as well the Rental Agreement clearly 
says that the “Damage rate” shall be Rs. 36 per kg but the Applicant 
Company/Operational Creditor has raised falsely the invoices on a 
higher rate of approximately Rs. 60 per kg, which is against the essence 
and spirit of the agreement clause, total material supplied amount has 
been calculated on a higher rate as well as the interest calculated on 
higher rate, the whole claim raised by the Applicant Company/ 
Operational Creditor is false and frivolous. 
ii. Failure to deduct the value of 11,570 kg of returned scaffolding material 
It is submitted that the Corporate Debtor has returned approx. 11570 kg 
of material to the Operational Creditor, which has not been deducted 
from the returned material amount value from the final bill and, also 
have calculated interest even on the returned material goods.

C.P.(IB)-28(ND)/2025 
Date of Order-02.12.2025 
Page 7 of 18  
iii. Raising of false invoices, supported by fabricated signatures and lack of 
delivery acknowledgments 
It is submitted that the Receiving Stock Challans (Challan No. 52, 57 and 
61) dated 12.07.2017, 21.07.2017 and 24.07.2017 respectively raise 
serious concern on the conduct of the Applicant Company/Operational 
Creditor. The Applicant Company/Operational Creditor has raised 
several false  invoices/challan against the Respondent Company/  
Corporate Debtor, few of the invoices dated 26.03.2022, 12.06.2018, 
15.06.2018, 30.07.2018 and 01.10.2018, bearing challan no 2021-
22/182, 119/32, 188/2018, 149/62 and 231/2018. The 
abovementioned false challans raised by the Applicant  
Company/Operational Creditor are of amount Rs. 3,24,540/- , Rs. 
2,26,150/-, Rs. 5,000/-, Rs. 15,000/-  and Rs. 4,37,750/-  (Total- Rs. 
10,08,440), the Applicant Company/Operational Creditor has also raised 
interest on the false challan from the date of issuance of the false 
Invoices/Challan. It is pertinent to highlight here  that the Respondent 
Company/Corporate Debtor has never received any material related to 
the abovementioned false Invoices/Challan. Further, the signatures have 
been used by the Respondent Company/Corporate Debtor to increase 
the final claim amount, there is no valid acknowledgement or receiving 
and Applicant Company/Operational Creditor has raised false and 
fabricated Invoices/Challans to defraud no only to the Respondent 
Company/Corporate Debtor but also to this Hon’ble Tribunal. 
iv. Supply of material worth only Rs. 18,06,377/- against agreed Rs. 
37,65,025/- showing breach by the Operational Creditor. 
It is submitted that as per the abovementioned Rental Agreement has 
agreed to supply the material worth of amount Rs. 37,65,025/- to the 
Respondent Company/ Corporate Debtor but the  Operational Creditor 
till 2022 has only supplied the material worth of amount Rs.18,06,377. 
The Applicant Company has failed to fulfil the agreed requirement as per 
the Rental Agreement and has raised misleading claim before this 
Adjudicating Authority.

C.P.(IB)-28(ND)/2025 
Date of Order-02.12.2025 
Page 8 of 18  
C.  NO DEFAULT IN OPERATIONAL DEBT 
It is submitted that the Petitioner is demanding payment based on inflated 
and forged invoices. Moreover, the cheque of Rs. 37,60,200/- was a security 
deposit, and not a payment toward operational debt, as per Clause 7 of the 
Rental Agreement dated 11.04.2016. It was to be adjusted against final bills 
after deducting returns and damages, which has not been done.  
      The Clause 7 of the agreement clearly says: - 
“The Lessee shall pay a security deposit to the Lessor as agreed 
upon at the time of signing of this agreement. The Lessee shall 
pay to the Lessor on demand from time to time additional 
proportionate amount for additional material taken on rent. The 
deposit will be adjusted against the “Final Bill” only. The Lessor 
will return to the Lessee any unused portion of the security 
deposit at the time this agreement is terminated. The security 
deposit shall not bear any interest.” 
D. SUPPRESSION OF MATERIAL FACTS AND FABRICATION 
It is submitted that the fabricated invoices dated 26.03.2022, 12.06.2018, 
15.06.2018, 30.07.2018, and 01.10.2018 bear no supporting stock entries 
or genuine acknowledgments. This vitiates the entire claim and amounts to 
fraud on this Adjudicating Authority. Reliance has been placed upon the 
case of Swiss Ribbons Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India, reported in (2019) 4 
SCC 17, wherein the Hon’ble Supreme Court  emphasized that IBC 
proceedings are not intended to be used by creditors acting in bad faith or 
with mala fide intentions. 
E. MATTER IS ALREADY SUB JUDICE ON THE SAME ISSUE 
It is submitted that the matter “M/s Cornish Aluminium India Pvt Ltd Vs. 
M/s Neo Nitika Project Pvt Ltd” (14 CC NI Act 40954/2022) already pending 
before the Dwaraka Court on the similar issue and the Petitioner has 
sought same relief before this Adjudicating Authority.

C.P.(IB)-28(ND)/2025 
Date of Order-02.12.2025 
Page 9 of 18  
13. ANALYSIS & FINDINGS 
 
i. We have heard the Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the Operational 
Creditor and the Corporate Debtor and perused the records. 
ii. The present application has been filed by the Applicant/Operational Creditor 
under Section 9 of IBC, 2016 seeking initiation of CIRP against M/s. Neo 
Nitika Projects Pvt Ltd, the Respondent/Corporate Debtor herein for an alleged 
default of Rs. 1,15,43,684.49/-. 
iii. This Adjudicating Authority vide Order dated 21.01.2025 directed the 
Applicant/Financial Creditor to file an affidavit with respect to the 
maintainability of the present application filed under Section 9 of IBC, 2016 
on the issue of threshold particularly with reference to the interest, within one 
week of the Order. The relevant portion of the Order is reproduced below: - 
“Learned Counsel appearing for the Applicant has submitted that the 
Applicant meets the threshold criteria for filing this application taking 
into account the principal as well as the interest amount. He shall file 
an affidavit with respect to the maintaina bility of the present 
application filed under Section 9 of IBC, 2016 on the issue of threshold 
particularly with reference to the interest, within one week.”  
iv. In compliance of Order dated 21.01.2025, the Applicant/Operational Creditor 
filed an affidavit dated 04.02.2025 and submitted that the present application 
filed under Section 9 of the Code, 2016 is maintainable as all the statutory 
requirements are fulfilled. The terms and conditions of the Rental Agreement 
dated 11.04.2016 explicitly mentions in Clause 6 that interest@ 24% per 
annum will be charged if the bill is not paid within credit period. The said 
invoices were duly received and acknowledged by the Corporate Debtor. As per 
the Certificate dated 24.01.2025 issued by Chartered Accountant confirming 
an operational debt amounting to Rs. 1,15,43,684.49/- is due on account of 
total rent receivable alongwith interest plus Rs. 18,06,377/- on account of loss 
of material value supplied to the Corporate Debtor) is payable to the Applicant 
Company by the Corporate Debtor.

C.P.(IB)-28(ND)/2025 
Date of Order-02.12.2025 
Page 10 of 18  
v. The Ld. Counsel appearing for the Respondent/Corporate Debtor submitted 
that as per the Financial Creditor’s own calculation, out of the alleged 
outstanding debt of Rs. 1,15,43,684.49/-, total outstanding due amount is 
only Rs. 55,56,311/- and total interest amount is Rs. 55,43,166/- and the 
amount due towards the material value excluding GST is Rs. 15,30,828/-. The 
claim amount is therefore, result of inflated calculation to meet the threshold 
amount of Rs. 1 Crore.  
vi. The issue to be examined in the present application is whether the 
outstanding debt amount meets the threshold as prescribed under Section 4 
of the Code, 2016 and whether the Corporate Debtor has raised a plausible 
dispute that existed prior to the receipt of Demand Notice dated 20.11.2023 
under Section 8(1) of the Code and truly exists in fact and is not spurious, 
hypothetical or illusory. 
vii. The Ld. Counsel for the Respondent submitted that the claim amount is 
unjustified and without any basis as the  claimed interest @ 24% per annum 
has been calculated on the basis of invoice which has been raised by the  
Financial Creditor which mentions interest @ 24% on every invoice. The 
Applicant Financial Creditor relied upon Clause 6 of the Rental Agreement 
dated 11.04.2016 wherein it has been mentioned that: -  
“If any charge is unpaid for 15 days from the date of bill for payment, 
then without prejudice to any other right or remedy, interest shall be 
charged at the rate of 24% per annum on the amount outstanding, 
calculated on a daily basis from the original due date until paid in full 
and compounded.”  
viii. It is submitted that the Operational Creditor intentionally to misguide this 
Adjudicating Authority have not mentioned Supplementary Agreement dated 
09.04.2016 signed between the parties at time of negotiation of the main 
agreement dated 11.04.2016 wherein, some conditions of the Rental 
Agreement were deleted and it has been mentioned that "the Condition No. 6.3, 
6.5, 6.8 & 8 of the rental agreement are hereby stand nullified".

C.P.(IB)-28(ND)/2025 
Date of Order-02.12.2025 
Page 11 of 18  
ix. It is further submitted that in Para 8(a) of the supplementary agreement it has 
also been stated that "An interest @ 12% shall be payable in case the payment 
not made within 45 days of presenting the R.A. Bill.". The contents of Para 8 
and Para 9 of the supplementary agreement make it amply clear that the rate 
of interest shall be 12% per annum charged after 45 days of submitting the 
R.A. Bill. However, the Operational Creditor  has calculated the interest @ 24% 
per annum apart from this in Para 2.1 of the Rental Agreement dated 
11.04.2016, it has been specifically mentioned that both the parties agree that 
this agreement will be exclusively meant for the sites specified by the lessee in 
the schedule attached to this agreement ....." so the interest @ 12% per annum 
shall be payable only for the site i.e. "Mahagun Mywood" mentioned in the 
Schedule attached to the rental agreement. However, the Operational Creditor 
deliberately in order to reach the threshold amount of 1 Crore has calculated 
the interest @ 24% per annum on bills of each and every site which is 
completely wrong as no interest has been agreed for any other site other than 
"Mahagun Mywood" and even the interest agreed in Mahagun Mywood is not 
more that 12% per annum. However, the Operational Creditor has deliberately 
calculated it on 24% per annum which is double the amount. 
x. It is further submitted that the perusal of the condition as contained in a 
typical invoice placed on record, i.e. " Interest @ 24% will be charged if bill is 
not paid within credit period". This clause of interest doesn't specify after how 
many days delayed payment interest is to be charged and on whether per 
annum or per month or any other period. This clause is non-specific as the 
time period is indefinite basis which the date of default has been arrived at. 
Furthermore, there is no agreement on record between the parties apart from 
the agreement dated 11.04.2016 which is meant specifically for "Mahagun 
Mywood" site as mentioned in the agreement itself in Para 2.1, and without 
any explicit agreement between the parties regarding levy of interest on 
delayed payment, just relying on a vague statement does not make it a 
contractual obligation.

C.P.(IB)-28(ND)/2025 
Date of Order-02.12.2025 
Page 12 of 18  
xi. The Ld. Counsel of the Respondent relied upon the judgment of Hon’ble NCLAT 
in the case of "Rishabh Infra Through Hari Mohan Gupta Vs. Sadbhav 
Engineering Ltd., reported in Company Appeal (AT) (Insolvency) No. 1881 of 
2024 decided on 04.11.2024 wherein Hon’ble Appellant Tribunal held that in 
the view that invoices which have been sent by the Operational Creditor 
containing the term of interest cannot be operated against the Corporate 
Debtor unless there is an agreement for interest or any other document 
showing that the Corporate Debtor has accepted the obligation for interest". 
However, in this case there is no agreement for interest except for one site i.e. 
Mahagun Mywood in which interest is @ 12% on delayed payments. 
xii. Similarly, the Appellate Tribunal in the case of SS Polymers vs Kanodia 
Technoplast Limited, had held that relying on the invoices to raise claims for 
payment of interest is against the principle of the Code. Relevant extracts from 
this judgment are reproduced herein:  
"4. The Learned Counsel for the Appellant relied on 'invoices' to suggest 
that in the 'invoices,' the claim was raised for payment of interest. 
However, we are not inclined to accept such submission as they were 
one side Invoices raised without any consent of the 'Corporate Debtor'.  
5. Admittedly, before the admission of an application under Section 9 of 
the Code, the 'Corporate Debtor' paid the total debt. The application 
was pursued for realisation of the interest amount, which, according 
to us is against the principle of the Code, as it should be treated to be 
an application pursued by the Applicant with malicious intent (to 
realise only Interest for any purpose other than for the Resolution of 
Insolvency, or Liquidation of the 'Corporate Debtor' and which is 
barred in view of Section 65 of the Code." Therefore, in the absence of 
any agreement between parties, regarding payment of interest on 
delayed payment, the claim with respect to interest on pending 
invoices is not sustainable, and on this ground the captioned 
Application is liable to be dismissed.”

C.P.(IB)-28(ND)/2025 
Date of Order-02.12.2025 
Page 13 of 18  
xiii. The Hon'ble Appellate Tribunal in Krishna Enterprises vs. Gammon India 
Ltd [Supra] held that ‘deb t’ in terms of the Code does not include interest, 
unless payable in terms of any agreement among parties. The relevant extract 
of the judgment passed by the Appellate Tribunal is reproduced below:  
"It is submitted that the 'debt' includes the interest, but such

xx. It is a well-settled law that interest cannot be fastened upon the Corporate 
Debtor unless there exists a specific contractual provision or any other 
document evidencing acknowledgment or acceptance by the Corporate Debtor 
to pay such interest. Upon careful perusal of the relevant provisions of the  
Rental Agreement dated 11.04.2016 and the Agreement dated 09.04.2016, it 
is observed that the parties have subsequently entered into a Supplementary 
Agreement, whereby Clauses 6.3, 6.5, 6.8, and 8 of the Rental Agreement 
which deals with the charging of interest were expressly nullified. In view 
thereof, the Applicant cannot claim interest on the alleged unpaid invoices, as 
there is no agreement between the parties providing for the same, except with 
respect to one particular site, namely “Mahagun Mywood,” where interest was 
specifically agreed at 12% per annum. 
xxi. Further, the rate of interest mentioned in the invoices filed along with the 
Application does not prescribe any time interval for its applicability nor 
clarifies whether such interest is to be computed per annum, per month, or 
otherwise. The clause, being vague and indefinite, fails to establish the exact 
point of default for computation of interest. Hence, in absence of any clear and 
explicit agreement apart from the Mahagun Mywood arrangement, the claim 
of the Applicant for interest on delayed payments is devoid of contractual 
foundation and cannot be sustained merely on the basis of a general or 
ambiguous statement. 
xxii. We are therefore, of considered view, that the Demand Notice dated 
20.11.2023 sent under Section 8(1) of the Code by the Applicant stipulating 
the alleged debt amount consists of inflated calculation of the Damage 
Rate/Loss rate despite agreeing on a much lesser amount and the Corporate 
Debtor as per the A greement between the parties and the Corporate Debtor 
has also raised a dispute regarding the bona fide of the invoices. After 
removing the inflated interest amount, the amount in the false invoices and 
proper calculation of the loss rate as has been agreed between the parties, the 
claim amount falls way below the basic threshold of 1 Crore as per Section 4 
of the Code.

xxiii. It is well settled that if the Corporate Debtor raises a plausible contention 
about a pre-existing dispute, which is not just a moonshine  or feeble legal 
argument it would suffice for the Adjudicating Authority to reject the 
application filed under Section 9 of the Code, the Adjudicating Authority being 
precluded from determining as to whether the Corporate Debtor would be 
successful or not, with regard to the said dispute, at the time of decision 
making.  
xxiv. In the facts and circumstances of the instant case, we are of the view that the 
Corporate Debtor has been able to raise a plausible contention regarding the 
pre-existence of “dispute” between the parties. 
14. Order 
In view of the above facts and circumstances and the foregoing discussion, we 
are satisfied that the present petition fails to fulfill the criteria laid down under 
Section 9 of the Code and therefore, is inadmissible. It is accordingly, hereby 
ordered as follows: - 
i. The Application bearing IB-28/ND/2025 filed by the Applicant under 
Section 9 of the Code r/w Rule 6 of the Adjudicating Authority Rules for 
initiating CIRP against the Respondent is hereby dismissed. 
ii. The Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the  Insolvency and 
Bankruptcy Board of India for their record.  
iii. A certified copy of this order may be issued, if applied for, upon compliance 
with all requisite formalities.
